newsitem.title: CUBA: Qatar considers economic accords with Cuba - paper.
newsitem.headline: Qatar considers economic accords with Cuba - paper.

text.p: The Gulf state of Qatar was studying the possibility of signing three economic accords with Cuba, including an investment promotion and protection agreement, a Cuban newspaper said on Sunday.

The business weekly Opciones quoted a senior Qatar government official, Mohamed Jiham al-Kawari, as saying the agreements under consideration also covered economic and technical cooperation and a reciprocal taxation accord.
Kawari, the Qatar Foreign Ministry's director for America and Europe, said during a visit to Cuba last week his country had already contracted the services of eight Cuban medical specialists.

Qatar was also considering cooperation with Cuba in the areas of sports and biotechnology, which could involve hiring Cuban coaches and purchasing Cuban-produced vaccines, Kawari was quoted as saying.
Another possibility was the establishment of flights by the Qatar national airline to Havana, Opciones said.

Qatar is rich in oil and gas reserves but the newspaper did not say if future bilateral cooperation could include shipments of Qatar crude oil to Cuba, which depends on oil imports for most of its energy needs.
The Cuban government had invited Qatar to attend as a guest a meeting of Caribbean states in Havana in December.
